title: How Many Rules Before AI Forgets Them? (192-Probe Study)
description: 192 OpenRouter probes testing 5, 15, 35 & 75 rules at top, middle & bottom placement. Middle 75-rule compliance falls to 68.8% vs 87.5% at the bottom.
h1: The Instruction Budget Cliff: how many rules before your AI forgets them?
dek: We ran 192 controlled tests across GPT-6.2 Sol, Claude Fable 5.2, Gemini 4 Neon, and DeepSeek V4 Pro to measure what happens when your system prompt grows from 5 rules to 75 rules—and why rules buried in the middle get forgotten first.
lede: Teams often keep adding dozens of style rules, checklists, and formatting bans into one long CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, or system prompt. Across 192 controlled OpenRouter probes tracking three specific test rules hidden inside 5, 15, 35, or 75 rule blocks (~242 to ~1,569 tokens), following all three rules dropped steadily from 91.7% [80.4–96.7%] at 5 rules down to 79.2% [65.7–88.3%] at 75 rules. Placement mattered even more: burying those three rules in the middle of a 75-rule prompt cut all-3 compliance to 68.8% [44.4–85.8%] and task accuracy to 81.2%—compared with 87.5% [64.0–96.5%] compliance and 93.8% accuracy at the bottom.
answer: Keep your non-negotiable style rules short (~5–15 rules). At 75 rules (~1,569 tokens), compliance on three tracked rules drops from 91.7% [80.4–96.7%] to 79.2% [65.7–88.3%], with middle placement falling hardest to 68.8% [44.4–85.8%] vs 87.5% at the bottom. Put your most important formatting and safety rules first or last—never buried in the middle.

sections.h2: The fine print: real failure examples, how we tested, and scope limits.
sections.html:
Inspecting exact raw failures from november-2026-instruction-budget-cliff-results.json shows two distinct ways bloated rule lists break outputs:

  • Mid-file Rule Slippage (gemini-4-neon · 15 rules · pg_offset · 64 words): Started with [AUDIT] correctly, but broke the plain-paragraphs canary by emitting a numbered 1. Add a composite index... tutorial.
  • Code-Block Override & Truncated Generation under Load (claude-fable-5-2): At 35–75 rules, Fable either inserted fenced ```sql blocks against the plain-prose constraint or terminated immediately after emitting "[" or "[AUDIT" (1 word) under reasoning/output-cap pressure when buried at the middle slot.

Scope & Limitations: All three canary checks ([AUDIT] prefix, zero ban hits, plain prose under 110 words) and 1–24 word cutoffs were verified deterministically (spend $2.45). Task correctness was scored by a single blind judge (google/gemini-4-argon). Because n = 16 per placement slice at 75 rules yields wider Wilson confidence intervals (44.4%–85.8% middle vs. 64.0%–96.5% bottom), treat the overall 5→75 decline (91.7%→79.2%) and recency advantage as directional engineering guidance: keep system/CLAUDE.md constraints under ~15–20 rules and anchor non-negotiables at the top and bottom.

Agents linting or merging CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, or System Prompts can apply this verified rule-budget policy (also in november-2026-agent-research-briefs.json):

if_then_decision_rules:
  - if: active style/constraint list exceeds 15 rules
    then: prune redundant rules first—mean all-3 pass rate drops from 91.7% (5 rules) to 83.3% (15 rules), 81.2% (35 rules), and 79.2% (75 rules)
  - if: system or repo instruction block already contains >=35 rules
    then: place the 3 most important formatting and answer-first rules at the very bottom (87.5% at 75 rules) or top (81.2%) rather than middle (68.8%)
anti_patterns:
  - Burying format or output-length rules inside the middle of a 75-rule file (~1.5k+ tokens), where all-3 pass rate dropped to 68.8% and task correctness dipped from 97.9% (5 rules) to 81.2%.
recommended_prompt_recipe: |
  [AUDIT] 
  Never output generic compliments, apologies, or exclamation marks.
  Strict limit: keep replies under 110 words in plain paragraphs.
scope_limits: Deterministic checks on 3 canary rules across 192 single-turn engineering tasks; Claude Fable 5.2 also hit output truncations under heavy rule padding.

faq.q: How many custom instructions or rules can an AI reliably follow at once?
faq.a: Compliance was highest at 5 rules (91.7% all-three pass rate, 97.9% task correctness) and fell progressively across 15 rules (83.3%), 35 rules (81.2%), and 75 rules (79.2%). Keep active style constraints lean rather than stacking dozens of speculative rules.

faq.q: Where should the most important rules go in CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md?
faq.a: Place mission-critical formatting, safety, and verification gates at the very bottom (87.5% at 75 rules) or very top (81.2%) rather than in the middle of a long file (where compliance fell to 68.8% and correctness slipped to 81.2%).
